newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's inland next target for investors - study.
newsitem.headline: China's inland next target for investors - study.

text.p: China's inland provinces are expected to be the next target for foreign direct investment, the Hong Kong government-funded Trade Development Council (TDC) said in a study released on Monday.

The booming coastal provinces, particularly Guangdong, adjacent to Hong Kong, and Fujian, across the strait from Taiwan, have enoyed the lion's share of direct foreign investment but the backward and poor inland provinces remain untapped, it said.

The TDC report said that, given the rich natural resources and increased investment incentives in inland regions, Hong Kong companies which target China's domestic market should consider venturing further into the hinterland.

In 1995, foreign direct investment in the central regions of China grew by 27.2 percent, exceeding the the national average growth rate of 11.7 percent. Direct investment in coastal regions grew 11.1 percent, it said.
Preferential financial treatment offered to investors may also boost foreign investment in the central and western regions of China, it said.

Benefits include gradually increasing the amount of tax refunds, assisting in the utilisation of local natural resources, and generous incentives and preferential treatment in export licenses and domestic sales to foreign companies, it said.
